sections.label: Singapore top Gallup law order
sections.summary: In 2020, Singapore ranked top in the Gallup Global Law and Order Report for the seventh year running.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: In 2020, Singapore was ranked top in the Gallup Global Law and Order Report for the seventh year running.

sections.label: Aims of the amendments
sections.summary: The amendments aim to enhance SPF's operational capabilities and readiness, improve its disciplinary, administrative and human resource processes, and strengthen controls over the Auxiliary Police Forces.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: The amendments aim to achieve the following: first, to enhance SPF's operational capabilities and readiness; second, to improve SPF's disciplinary, administrative and human resource processes; and third, to strengthen controls over the Auxiliary Police Forces.

sections.label: Penalties for evading roadblock
sections.summary: Clause 6 increases the maximum jail term and fine for evading a Police roadblock to increase deterrence.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: To increase deterrence, clause 6 of the Bill increases the maximum jail term and fine for evading a Police roadblock.

sections.label: Police forced entry life-saving power
sections.summary: Clause 7 makes explicit that Police officers may forcibly enter any place if they reasonably suspect a person needs assistance due to injury or poor health.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: To provide Police officers with greater assurance that they can make forced entry to conduct life-saving operations, clause 7 makes explicit that Police officers have the power to make forced entry of any place if they reasonably suspect that a person requires assistance because of injury or poor health.

sections.label: SPO powers same as regulars
sections.summary: Clause 10 provides SPOs with the same powers conferred on regulars to close the gap.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: To close this gap, clause 10 provides SPOs with the same powers conferred on regulars.

sections.label: CAO search arrest bail powers
sections.summary: Clause 9 gives CAOs more powers, including arresting persons possessing anything reasonably suspected to be fraudulently obtained and issuing bails and bonds.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: However, if the suspect is unable to furnish bail and is subject to lock-up, CAOs will have to seek the assistance of Police officers to search the suspect to remove illicit items or items that may be used to facilitate escape or cause harm, prior to the lock-up.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: Hence, clause 9 provides CAOs with more powers, such as the power to arrest persons who possess anything reasonably suspected to be fraudulently obtained, and the power to issue bails and bonds.

sections.label: Commissioner delegation to civilian officers
sections.summary: Clause 5 lets the Commissioner delegate his and his Deputy Commissioners' powers to civilian officers in leadership positions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: Clause 5 allows the Commissioner to delegate his and his Deputy Commissioners' powers to civilian officers in leadership positions.

sections.label: Liability protection for officers
sections.summary: Clause 27 protects Police officers, SPOs, CAOs, Intelligence Officers and Forensic Specialists from liability for good faith acts and omissions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: Clause 27 protects Police officers, SPOs, CAOs, Intelligence Officers and Forensic Specialists from liability for acts and omissions done in good faith and with reasonable care.

sections.label: Resignation refusal during crisis
sections.summary: Clause 3 provides that the Commissioner may refuse a notice of resignation given during a crisis period.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: To make sure that SPF has sufficient manpower resources during a major crisis, clause 3 provides that the Commissioner may refuse a notice of resignation given during a crisis period.

sections.label: Higher fines for officers
sections.summary: Clauses 8 and 15 increase the maximum fines for Volunteer Special Constabulary Officers and regular Police Officers below Inspector rank.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: First, clauses 8 and 15 increase the maximum fines for Volunteer Special Constabulary Officers and regular Police Officers below the rank of Inspector.

sections.label: Disbanding VC, transferring officers
sections.summary: MHA will disband the VC and transfer all existing VC officers to the Special Constabulary.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: Moving forward, MHA will be disbanding the VC and transferring all existing VC officers to the Special Constabulary.

sections.label: Approvals for APF employers
sections.summary: Clause 21 requires approval from the Minister and Commissioner for APF employer acquisitions, chairmen and directors, and clause 22 requires controller notifications and approvals.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: First, before a person acquires the business of an APF employer, clause 21 requires both the person and the APF employer to seek approval from the Minister.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: Second, clause 21 will require the chairman and directors of an APF employer to be approved by the Commissioner of Police, on top of the existing requirement for the CEO to be approved.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: Third, clause 22 will require a person to notify the Commissioner after becoming a 5% controller of an APF employer and to seek the Minister’s approval before becoming a 25%, 50% or indirect controller, or ceasing to be a 50% or 75% controller.

sections.label: Special administration order for APF employers
sections.summary: Clause 24 lets the Minister issue a special administration order for an APF employer's affairs to be managed by the Commissioner or an appointed person, and MHA will update penalties.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: Clause 24 provides for the Minister to issue a special administration order to allow the affairs of an APF employer to be managed by the Commissioner or an appointed person.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: MHA will also update the penalties for offences and infringements in relation to APF employers and controllers.

sections.label: Police officers' personal liability protection
sections.summary: Section 114A now explicitly affirms the protection of Police officers from personal liability.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Section 114A now explicitly affirms the protection of Police officers from personal liability.

sections.label: Penalty for evading road barrier
sections.summary: Under section 26(8)(a), evading a road barrier carries a fine of up to $10,000, imprisonment of up to seven years, or both.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Under section 26(8)(a), a person guilty of evading a road barrier faces a fine of up to $10,000, imprisonment of up to a term of seven years, or both.

sections.label: Minimum punishment and APF employer liability
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Ministry could impose a minimum punishment, including mandatory jail, for evading road barriers, and raises APF employer liability under section 87(9).

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Could the Ministry consider imposing a minimum punishment, including a mandatory jail term, for evading road barriers?

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: My next suggestion relates to the liability of employers of Auxiliary Police Forces, or APFs, under section 87(9).

sections.label: Delegating CP or DCP powers
sections.summary: Clause 5 changes the position to enable powers of the CP or DCP to be delegated to non-Police personnel performing Police Force duties not below the prescribed grade.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Clause 5 of the Bill will change the position to enable such powers of the CP or DCP to be delegated to non-Police personnel who are performing duties in the Police Force not below the prescribed grade.

sections.label: Changes to roadblock provision
sections.summary: Clause 6 of the Bill makes changes to the provision on conducting roadblocks.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Clause 6 of the Bill makes changes to the provision on conducting roadblocks.

sections.label: CAO and SPO powers
sections.summary: Clauses 9 and 10 expand CAO and SPO powers to all Police powers, including arrest without warrant, search and forced entry.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Clauses 9 and 10 of the Bill propose to expand the powers of CAOs and Special Police Officers (SPOs).

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: These clauses will empower these officers not just to do investigations but to exercise all Police powers, including the power of arrest without warrant, and have similar powers of search, forced entry and so on.

sections.label: Family violence case increase
sections.summary: The Minister of State for Home Affairs said family violence cases rose 10% monthly between April and December last year.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Just in January this year, the Minister of State for Home Affairs Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim had said there was a 10% increase in family violence cases every month between April and December last year.

sections.label: Toa Payoh forced entry incident
sections.summary: Officers forced into a Toa Payoh flat after a 64-year-old man threatened suicide and allegedly stabbed an officer.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: For example, in February, officers had to force their way into a Toa Payoh flat after a 64-year-old man locked himself in his room and threatened to commit suicide.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The man charged towards the officers and allegedly stabbed a Police officer in the thigh.

sections.label: Roadblock operations and offenders
sections.summary: The passage asks how many roadblock operations occurred in the last five years and how many offenders were caught.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In the last five years, how many roadblock operations were there and how many offenders had been caught?

sections.label: Advertising restrictions on APFs
sections.summary: New section 86A restricts advertising so only an APF may advertise or hold out that it carries on APF functions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: A second area is the introduction as a new section 86A of restrictions on advertising, where only an APF may carry on the functions of an APF and advertise or, in any other way, hold out that it carries on or is willing to carry on the functions of an APF.

sections.label: Special Administration Order for APFs
sections.summary: New Division 1C allows transfer of APF management to the Commissioner or Minister's appointee in specified situations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The third set of amendments introduces under the New Division 1C of Part IX, a Special Administration Order or other order to transfer management of an APF from an employer to the Commissioner or anyone appointed by the Minister.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This can be done in situations where the employer is unable to pay its debts, during a public emergency, or when the Minister deems it in the public interest.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The utility of our APFs was made apparent recently, as Certis took up duties urgently needed for the issuance, enforcement and execution of quarantine orders and quarantine operations of the Ministry of Health (MOH).

sections.label: Delegation to civilian officers
sections.summary: The CP may currently delegate CP and DCP powers only to Police officers in leadership positions, but amendments allow delegation to civilian officers in leadership positions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Currently, the CP may only delegate his and the DCP's powers to Police officers in leadership positions within SPF.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: However, with the new amendments, the CP is empowered to delegate CP and DCP powers to civilian officers in leadership positions within SPF.

sections.label: Protection from liability for officers
sections.summary: The amendment makes explicit protection from liability for officers acting in good faith and with reasonable care, codifying and enhancing existing common law protection.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: The amendment also seeks to "Make explicit the protection for Police officers, Special Police officers (SPOs), Commercial Affairs officers (CAOs), Intelligence Officers and Forensic Specialists from liability for acts and omissions done in good faith and with reasonable care." Currently, our officers rely on the defence of necessity under common law.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: The amendment seeks to codify and enhance existing protection for our officers in their execution of the Police Force Act (PFA) or any other written law.

sections.label: Balancing protection with stiffer penalties
sections.summary: Protection from liability for good faith acts must be balanced with stiffer penalties if this protection is abused by errant officers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: While we increase the protection to our officers, we must never allow errant officers who act inappropriately to hide behind this.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Hence, the protection from liability in the act of good faith must be balanced with stiffer penalties if this is abused.

sections.label: Protecting officers acting in good faith
sections.summary: The amendment protects and reassures officers acting in good faith with care, while irresponsible and errant officers must not escape punishment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: The victim may or may not have survived, but should we not protect our officer for acting in good faith and using as much care as he possibly could at that moment?

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: This amendment will, undoubtedly, protect and reassure our officers as they carry out their duties.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: As we enhance and strengthen protection for our officers, we must never allow irresponsible and errant officers to escape punishment.

sections.label: Keeping Singapore safe and secure
sections.summary: The amendments will enable SPF to continue keeping Singapore safe and secure amidst an increasingly complex operating environment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: The amendments will enable SPF to continue keeping Singapore safe and secure amidst an increasingly complex operating environment.

sections.label: Forced entry for assistance
sections.summary: New section 26E allows a Police officer to force entry on reasonable suspicion that assistance may be required for injury or poor health.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The new section 26E will allow a Police officer to force entry into a place on reasonable suspicion that assistance may be required for injury or poor health to protect the life, health or safety of the person.

sections.label: Expanded Police powers in Bill
sections.summary: The Bill's amendments expand the Police powers of Special Police Officers and Commercial Affairs Officers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The amendments in this Bill expand the Police powers of the Special Police Officers and Commercial Affairs Officers.

sections.label: Refusing police resignation notices
sections.summary: New section 13A lets the Commissioner of Police refuse a Police officer's resignation notice during a crisis period.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The new section 13A provides that a notice to resign from SPF given by a Police officer may be refused by the Commissioner of Police during a crisis period.

sections.label: Question on refusing resignations
sections.summary: A question asks the Minister of State what extreme circumstances would lead the Police Commissioner to refuse resignation notices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Minister of State share in what extreme circumstances do we envision the Police Commissioner refusing such notices to resign?

sections.label: Higher penalties for evading roadblocks
sections.summary: The Bill raises penalties for evading roadblocks to a maximum seven years' jail and/or S$10,000 fine.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: The Bill proposes to increase the penalties for evading roadblocks from the current maximum jail term of 12 months and/or fine of S$5,000 to a maximum jail term of seven years and/or fine of S$10,000.

sections.label: More powers for CAOs
sections.summary: The Bill gives CAOs more Police powers, including arrest, entering places to investigate arrestable offences and requiring suspects to attend Court.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: The Bill proposes to provide CAOs with more Police powers, such as the power to arrest, to enter a place to investigate an arrestable offence and requiring suspects to attend Court, among others.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: This is a significant extension of Police powers to civilian officers and possibly unprecedented.

sections.label: Powers of PNSFs and PNSmen
sections.summary: The Bill proposes to expand the powers of Police full-time National Servicemen and Police reservists.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: The Bill also proposes to expand the powers of our Police full-time National Servicemen (PNSFs) and Police reservists (PNSmen).

sections.label: Deploying NSFs to SPF
sections.summary: MINDEF's Cyber NSF Scheme is cited as an example of matching national servicemen's backgrounds to vocations such as Cyber Operator and SPF cybersecurity teams.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: One good example is the MINDEF's Cyber NSF Scheme, which I believe the Minister of State would be familiar with.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: It allows those with cybersecurity and computer science backgrounds to apply for a vocation as a Cyber Operator during their National Service.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Perhaps those with law or finance backgrounds can be deployed to the Commercial Affairs Department while those with computer science training can be deployed to help strengthen the SPF's cybersecurity teams.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: We should strive to leverage the strengths and talents of our PNSFs and PNSmen to augment the good work of our regular Police officers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: But as we expand the powers of various categories of officers, we must ensure that we are able to continue to attract the best candidates to perform the specialist roles in SPF.

sections.label: Roadblock evasion cases
sections.summary: From 2016 to 2020, SPF ran about 8,000 roadblocks yearly, with 33 evasion cases convicted or warned, two causing officer injury.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: From 2016 to 2020, SPF conducted about 8,000 roadblocks per year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: There were 33 cases of roadblock evasion where the offender was convicted or issued with a stern warning.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: Of these, there were two cases where the roadblock evasion directly resulted in injury for Police officers.

sections.label: Higher roadblock evasion penalties
sections.summary: The Bill increases penalties significantly to strengthen deterrence against roadblock evasion given the high risks.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: Given the high risks, the Bill increases the penalties significantly to strengthen the deterrence against roadblock evasion.

sections.label: Police first aid skills
sections.summary: All frontline Police officers have basic first aid and CPR skills and must undergo regular recertification to keep them up-to-date.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: All frontline Police officers are equipped with basic first aid and CPR skills and are required to undergo regular recertification to ensure their skills remain up-to-date and relevant.

sections.label: Forced entry liability protection
sections.summary: Officers making forced entry in attempted suicide cases are protected under common law necessity and will remain protected under new section 114A of the PFA.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: Police officers who make forced entry in cases of attempted suicide are already protected from liability under the common law defence of necessity and will continue to be protected in future for acts done in good faith and with reasonable care, when the new section 114A of the PFA comes into effect.

sections.label: CAD officer composition
sections.summary: CAD comprises about 130 CAOs and 90 regular Police officers, figures stable over five years with generally low new CAO attrition.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: On Mr Yong's suggestion to deploy regular Police officers, CAD already comprises a mix of CAOs and regular Police officers, as Ms Lim has also pointed out.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: There are currently about 130 CAOs and 90 regular Police officers in CAD.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: These figures have remained stable in the last five years and the attrition rate for new CAOs has generally been low.

sections.label: Training adequate for CAOs
sections.summary: Training is assessed as adequate for operational needs, so no IPPT or PES requirement is set for CAOs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: For now, we assess that the training is adequate to meet our operational needs and it is not necessary to set an IPPT or PES requirement for CAOs.

sections.label: SPOs and CAOs training
sections.summary: SPOs and CAOs must undergo rigorous training and tests before exercising policing powers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: First, SPOs and CAOs will be required to undergo rigorous training and tests before they can exercise policing powers.

sections.label: SPF zero tolerance misuse
sections.summary: SPF has zero tolerance for persons who misuse or abuse their policing powers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: Third, SPF has zero tolerance for persons who misuse or abuse their policing powers.

sections.label: Delegation of policing powers
sections.summary: Delegation of powers will be carefully considered, and highly sensitive powers are non-delegable to Police or civilian officers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: We want to assure the House that the delegation of powers will be carefully considered in the best way possible to achieve our desired outcomes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: It is provided in law that highly sensitive powers which should only be exercised by the Commissioner himself will be non-delegable to either Police officers or even civilian officers.

sections.label: SPF diversity and transformation
sections.summary: This enables SPF to be more diverse, agile and open to transformation, and clause 5 does not let civilian officers exercise the Commissioner's frontline command powers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: This enables SPF to be more diverse, agile and open to transformation and to better achieve its mission of ensuring the safety and security of Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: That said, I would like to assure Ms Sylvia Lim that the intent of clause 5 of the Bill is not to allow civilian officers to exercise the Commissioner's powers of command at the frontline.

sections.label: CAD civilian officers investigate crimes
sections.summary: SPF's Commercial Affairs Department already has civilian officers with powers to investigate commercial and financial crimes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: Mr Sharael Taha also asked if the Commissioner will delegate the power to investigate commercial, financial and cybercrimes to civilian officers, given the recent uptick in such crimes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: I want to clarify that SPF’s Commercial Affairs Department already has civilian officers who have the powers to investigate such commercial and financial crimes.

sections.label: Refusing notices of resignation
sections.summary: Notices of resignation can be refused only when the President has issued a Proclamation of Emergency over a grave emergency threatening Singapore's security or economic life.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: To recap, as set out in the Bill, notices of resignation can be refused only under two situations.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: First, when the President has issued a Proclamation of Emergency under the Constitution, when she is satisfied that a grave emergency exists whereby the security or economic life of Singapore is threatened.

sections.label: Police forced entry without verification
sections.summary: Police officers who force entry to arrest a suspect without first verifying he was inside would not have acted in good faith and with reasonable care.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: First, if Police officers receive a tip-off that a suspect of a crime is in a building and immediately effect forced entry to arrest him without even first attempting to verify if he was actually inside, the Police officers would not have acted in good faith and with reasonable care.

sections.label: Making Police uniforms without permission
sections.summary: A person who manufactures Police uniforms without the Commissioner's permission is liable for a fine not exceeding $10,000 or up to three years' jail, or both.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: Should a person manufacture Police uniforms without the Commissioner’s permission, he will be liable for a fine not exceeding $10,000 or jailed for up to three years, or both.

sections.label: Controller notification and approval requirements
sections.summary: A person must notify the Commissioner after becoming a 5% controller of an APF employer and seek the Minister's approval for 25%, 50% or indirect controller status.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: As Mr Raj Joshua Thomas has also commented on the controller requirements, I would like to reiterate that the requirements are for a person to notify the Commissioner after becoming a 5% controller of an APF employer and to seek the Minister's approval before becoming a 25%, 50% or indirect controller or ceasing to be a 50% or 75% controller.

sections.label: Offence of unauthorised security activity
sections.summary: Clause 20 makes it an offence for a person who is not an employer of an authorised APF to carry out security activity in the course of business, with updated penalties.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas commented on clause 20 of the Bill, which makes it an offence for a person, who is not an employer of an authorised APF, to carry out any security activity in the course of any business.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: Such a provision is currently covered under the existing section 86(9), but we have updated the penalties.
